item.title: CrowdStrike Reaches $44 Billion CyberSecurity Deal for Zscaler
item.description: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. has agreed to acquire cybersecurity provider Zscaler Inc. in one of the largest-ever deals in the sector.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould and David Carnevali

item.title: German Billionaires Who Backed BioNTech Are Investing in Catalym
item.description: Catalym GmbH, a closely held cancer-treatments company based near Munich, has found some well-heeled backers.
item.dc:creator: Sonja Wind and Arno Schütze

item.title: US Market in for 'Pretty Painful Ride,' Pickering Says
item.description:
Kallum Pickering, chief economist at Peel Hunt, says US markets are going to have a "pretty painful ride," and the Federal Reserve will need to scale back its rate-hike expectations. "Into next year, we'll start repositioning away from the US towards the companies that can use this stuff," he tells Bloomberg Television. Pickering adds a 50 bps rate hike from the Fed in December would be a "big mistake," and instead he expects one other increase early next year.
Original filename: 20261123_093704_Pickering_Sees_Painful_US_Market_Ride_as_Tightening_Hits_Ove.mp4 (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Futures Rally Following AI Selloff, Havens Decline
item.description: US equity-index futures rallied as buyers returned after Friday’s AI selloff. US Treasury futures declined as demand for havens waned on signs that the recent selloff in equities may be drawing some buyers back. Bloomberg's Ruhell Amin breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What a Town of Vibecoders Says About the Chinese Economy
item.description: According to Stanford's AI Index, 84% of people surveyed in China say they are optimistic about AI. In the US, by contrast, 38% of those surveyed say they are optimistic. That's a big gulf in enthusiasm, and you can see it borne out in the stories you read: While in the US we hear about AI doomsday scenarios, in China, you'll hear about grandmas who are obsessed with using OpenClaw. Afra Wang has spent a lot of time in mainland China reporting from the country's AI hotbed — in a vibecoding-obsessed town outside of Hangzhou; at the for-profit schools where influencers are teaching everyday people how to use the technology; and the content studios that are pumping out AI microdramas. She understands, better than most, how AI is reshaping everyday life in China, and for today's episode, we talk to her about her reporting on AI in China and how the technology is actually diffusing into Chinese society. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Plug-In Solar Is Sweeping the US
item.description: US electricity prices have climbed since 2020 and the federal tax credit for rooftop solar is gone. Can a $300 plug-in solar panel give Americans a little more control over their electricity bills? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia-Backed AI Company Firmus Mulls $1.5 Billion Bond Offering
item.description: Artificial intelligence company Firmus Grid Ltd. is considering seeking around $1.5 billion in a bond offering that would be part of a larger debt financing deal, according to people familiar with the matter, after it shelved plans for an initial public offering last month.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang, Sheryl Tian Tong Lee and Megawati Wijaya

item.title: China’s Next AI Deals Clouded by Selloff After Anthropic IPO
item.description: A selloff in global stocks that’s accelerated since the record US initial public offering of Anthropic PBC is clouding the outlook for the next wave of share sales by China’s artificial intelligence champions.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Shoprite Buys DNI Stake to Grow Fintech, Mobile Through Partnership With Investec
item.description: Shoprite Holdings Ltd. and Investec are deepening bets on fintech and mobile services as Africa’s biggest supermarket retailer buys a stake in technology, hardware and financing firm DN Invest Ltd.
item.dc:creator: Loni Prinsloo and Janice Kew

item.title: How Trump’s AI Chip Crackdown May Hit Southeast Asia
item.description:
Washington’s AI chip crackdown spells trouble for a multibillion dollar cloud business helping to power Southeast Asia’s data center boom.
The new rulebook applies to data centers in places like Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia. Newley Purnell has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What’s Next for AI Trade & Asia Tech Stocks?
item.description: James Sullivan, Co-Head of Global Fundamental Research at JPMorgan, says Asian AI stocks are pricing in earnings cuts of as much as 30%, while the firm sees about 5% as realistic. On Bloomberg's Insight with Haslinda Amin, he discussed the recent tech selloff, as well as his outlook for Fed policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Defense AI Startup Agon Raises $70 Million Series A From VCs, ex-Sequoia Boss
item.description: Agon, a UK startup that makes simulation software for the European defense industry, has raised $70 million from investors including Sequoia Capital’s former head Roelof Botha.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen

item.title: The Bull Case for Britain
item.description: When it comes to the UK economy, the prevailing mood has been decidedly downbeat. But Morgan Stanley’s Chief UK Economist, Bruna Skarica, sees reasons to be more optimistic — from improving productivity and the potential benefits of AI adoption to signs of resilience among UK households and businesses. In this episode, Skarica joins host Merryn Somerset Webb to make the case for a more constructive outlook. They discuss the UK’s fiscal risks, what’s driving the recent improvement in productivity, whether AI could ultimately translate into higher wages and living standards and what a stronger economy could mean for UK markets over the next five years. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ING's Sareen: Asia AI Chip Demand Unlikely to Crash
item.description: ING Chief Executive and Head of Wholesale Banking for APAC Uday Sareen says US export controls may create investment uncertainty, but are unlikely to trigger a sharp drop in AI chip demand. He adds that Southeast Asia’s data-center buildout remains intact, though growth could moderate. Sareen speaks with Haslinda Amin on "Insight with Haslinda Amin." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: WeRide CEO on Earnings and International Markets
item.description: Tony Han, CEO at WeRide, discusses the company’s third-quarter results and its partnership with Uber to expand its robotaxi services in international markets. He speaks exclusively on "Bloomberg: The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US AI Chip Curbs Test Southeast Asia Data Center Boom
item.description: Washington’s new rulebook for export control of chips spells trouble for a multibillion dollar cloud business helping to power Southeast Asia's data center boom. Bloomberg’s Kari Soo Lindberg breaks down the potential disruption and says companies seeking computing capacity may turn to other regions in the future. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How to Find Value as the AI Trade Unravels
item.description: Eva Lee, Chief Investment Office Head of Greater China Equities at UBS Global Wealth Management, says investors can look to companies with strong balance sheets, sound fundamentals and capacity for buybacks. Investor sentiment toward the AI trade remains fragile even after Asian authorities rolled out support measures and US markets showed signs of stabilizing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Set to Erase 2026 Gains on AI Selloff
item.description: Emerging-market stocks are set to erase this year’s gains as mounting concerns over the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence trade fuel a global selloff stretching from the US to Asia.
item.dc:creator: Prima Wirayani

item.title: AI Investment Adding to Inflation: Jain
item.description: Illiana Jain, International Economist at Westpac, says further rate hikes are expected from the Fed in a bid to get a hold on inflation. James says investment in the AI sector reflects a weakness in broader investment outside the sector. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ant Group Bets on Simplexity in China’s Humanoid Race
item.description: Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics received $100 million in a funding round led by Jack Ma-backed Ant Group Co., betting that the startup can take on more established players in the country’s burgeoning robotics arena.
item.dc:creator: Saritha Rai
